summary: SCIM PATCH Content-Type discrepancy causes role cache divergence and intermittent 403s for recently deprovisioned admins
description: Customer reports intermittent 403s for users whose admin role was removed in the IdP. The deprovisioning event is visible in the customer's SCIM logs, but Redwood's role cache retains the admin binding for ~30-90s causing a short window of authorization flip (allowed -> denied) depending on which token/session path is used. This is causing automated job failures and confusion during immediate post-deprovision operations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In customer's IdP (SCIM provisioning), remove 'platform-admin' role from a user via PATCH request (delta) rather than full replace.
2) IdP sends SCIM PATCH to Redwood SCIM endpoint with Content-Type: application/scim+json; charset=UTF-8
3) Observe SCIM PATCH accepted (201/204) in customer's provisioning logs and in Redwood intake logs
4) Immediately attempt admin API call with an existing session token or perform console action: some requests succeed, some return 403 within the first ~90s post-deprovision.
5) After ~2 minutes, all requests consistently return 403 as expected.
logs: <api> 2026-03-12T15:08:12.475Z request_id=req_9fc call=admin.create-invite user=84a1 result=403 code=forbidden msg=User lacks platform-admin
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: role-cache invalidation job not triggered for SCIM PATCH requests that carry 'charset' in Content-Type header. Our SCIM intake codec compares exact Content-Type values when selecting delta parser path.

Reproduced in internal staging by sending PATCH with 'application/scim+json; charset=UTF-8' — observed the SCIM delta handler fell back to generic ingest pipeline that writes a 'provision_event' but does not call cacheInvalidator.notifyUserChange().

Observed two different authorization evaluation paths: live session requests sometimes short-circuit to token-bound cached roles (fast-path) and do not re-check provisioner state until token refresh; API calls that trigger a synchronous re-eval hit the updated state sooner. This explains the interleaving of ALLOW then DENY behavior.
Customer SCIM logs show IdP (ForgeOnPrem) switched library version in last week to include charset in Content-Type for PATCH requests. No changes in payload body.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Support: Ava Chen: Thanks for the report and logs. We're starting an investigation focused on SCIM intake Content-Type handling and role-cache invalidation. We've escalated to infra.

2026-03-12 - Eng (Marco Ruiz): Reproduced locally with curl sending Content-Type: application/scim+json; charset=UTF-8. We see the delta parser not selected due to strict header match. Working on a patch to normalize Content-Type parsing and trigger immediate cache invalidation for affected user entries.

2026-03-13 - Support: Communicated workaround to customer: request IdP team to send full-replace (PUT) for role removals, or temporarily add 2-minute drain window to critical jobs. Customer accepted workaround.
2026-03-14 - Eng: Created PR to make Content-Type matching tolerant and add idempotent cacheInvalidator.notifyUserChange() on delta path. Running internal tests and will roll to canary tomorrow.
resolution: Rolling patch deployed to canary (scim-intake v2.3.8) which normalizes Content-Type header matching (ignores charset and parameter order) and ensures delta PATCH flows call cacheInvalidator.notifyUserChange(user_id). After canary validation, the fix will be rolled to prod. Workaround previously provided: have IdP send PUT or wait 2 minutes before relying on deprovisioned privileges.
